summary: Hakai Passage Water Aerodrome (YHC) is a remote seaplane base situated on Hecate Island along British Columbia's Central Coast. It serves as an access point for the Hakai Luxvbalis Conservancy Area, one of the largest protected marine regions on Canada's Pacific coast. The facility primarily supports float-equipped aircraft servicing fishing lodges, ecological research stations, and adventure tourism in this rugged, sparsely populated archipelago.
faqs:
Q: What type of aircraft can use Hakai Passage Water Aerodrome?
A: Only float-equipped (seaplane) aircraft can land here, as it is a water aerodrome with no runway infrastructure.

Q: Are there scheduled commercial flights to YHC?
A: Scheduled service is limited; most flights are charter operations arranged through lodges or outfitters serving the Central Coast region.

Q: What facilities are available at the aerodrome?
A: As a remote water aerodrome, it offers minimal infrastructure—primarily a sheltered waterway for landing. Passengers should arrange ground logistics in advance through their charter operator or lodge.

Q: When is the best time to fly to Hakai Passage?
A: The summer months (June through September) offer the calmest weather and longest daylight hours, which are ideal for floatplane operations in this exposed coastal area.
transport_tips: Access to YHC is exclusively by floatplane, typically departing from Vancouver, Campbell River, or Port Hardy on Vancouver Island. Visitors must pre-arrange charter flights and confirm luggage weight limits, as small floatplanes have strict payload capacities. There are no roads connecting Hecate Island to mainland infrastructure, so all onward travel requires pre-booked boat transfers.
local_tip: Tides in the Hakai Passage region are extreme—often exceeding 15 feet—so ask your pilot about optimal landing windows tied to tidal currents, which can affect water conditions at the touchdown zone.
